# `silk/text/vertical_text`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Character orientation in vertical text (UAX #50), with data from Unicode 18.0.0.

## When to use
Use [`orientations`](#orientations) to lay out vertical text, such as vertical Japanese: it splits the text
into runs that stand upright and runs that are rotated.

## Details
The orientation belongs to a whole extended grapheme cluster, so combining marks and emoji
sequences never split. An enclosing mark makes its cluster upright. The runs are byte ranges of
the text, appended to a caller-owned list.

## Gotchas
The result is the fallback orientation, without font data. A character with
`Vertical_Orientation` `Tu` or `Tr` needs its vertical alternate glyph when the font has one.
Read `VerticalOrientation.of` in `silk.text.unicode_properties` for that.

## Examples
### Find the rotated part of vertical text
```silk
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.text.vertical_text
import silk.text.vertical_text { Orientation, OrientationRun }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut runs = List<OrientationRun>.make()
  // Two kanji, then Latin letters.
  run vertical_text.orientations("\u{65e5}\u{672c}abc", &mut runs)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let items = runs.asSlice()
  if items.length != 2 || items[0].orientation != Orientation.Upright || items[1].start != 6
    || items[1].orientation != Orientation.Rotated {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `vertical_text` with `import silk.text.vertical_text as vertical_text`.

<a id="orientations"></a>

## `orientations`

```silk
pub effect fn orientations(text: string, output: &mut List<OrientationRun>) -> ()
  ! OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends the runs of fallback orientation of `text` for vertical layout to `output`.

### Details

The orientation follows UAX #50 for whole extended grapheme clusters: the first scalar of a
cluster decides, but an enclosing mark (General_Category `Me`) makes the cluster upright.
`Vertical_Orientation` `U` and `Tu` give [`Orientation.Upright`](#Orientation.Upright), and `R` and `Tr` give
[`Orientation.Rotated`](#Orientation.Rotated). The runs are not empty, they cover the text in order without gaps, and
empty text gives none. The function does not clear `output`, so clear it first to reuse its
storage.

### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow `output`.

### Gotchas

`Tu` and `Tr` characters need a vertical alternate glyph when the font has one; the fallback
orientation applies only without it. Read `VerticalOrientation.of` in
`silk.text.unicode_properties` to tell them apart from `U` and `R`.
